summary: Rapid queue growth and p99 latency spikes during reserved pool rebalancing
description:
Issue summary: HelixBio reported a sudden increase in request queue depth for their dedicated reserved pool starting ~2026-03-10T08:12Z. P99 generation latency rose from ~120ms to >2.4s for short inference requests, and the pool reported intermittent GPU allocation failures.

Impact: Customer's user-facing product experienced degraded responsiveness for ~45 minutes, causing failed UX flows and throttled retry storms. This affected a single reserved capacity contract (dedicated) and impacted two commonly used model routes.

Environment: prod us-east-1, dedicated pool: pool-helix-3, autoscaler: rebalancer-v2 (enabled), serving-runtime: 1.34.2.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run many short, low-token inference requests from a noisy tenant simultaneously (observed from tenant id noisy-tenant-47).
2) Trigger scheduled rebalancer cycle (rebalancer runs every 60s by default).
3) Observe queue depth metric climb and GPU allocation latency metrics tick up within the same rebalancer cycle window.

Observed behavior: During rebalancer cycles, allocation churn increases (frequent GPU handoffs), concurrent short jobs from another tenant are scheduled onto the same nodes, runtime reports increased kvcache eviction and binding latency. The scheduler queues for HelixBio's routes grow rapidly and p99 latency spikes. We also saw a correlated rise in the rebalancer_cycle_count and gpu_alloc_failures metrics.

Expected behavior: Rebalancer should avoid causing immediate allocation churn under transient short-job pressure and preserve steady allocation for reserved tenants. P99 should remain within SLA thresholds for pinned model routes.

Logs / Dashboards:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pool_metrics/pool-helix-3?orgId=1
- Allocation trace: s3://redwood-logs/pool-helix-3/2026-03-10/rebalancer-trace.log
- Serving runtime logs (sample): https://logs.redwood.ai/serving/runtime/pool-helix-3/2026-03-10

Attachments: heap of short traces attached to ticket (key traces: trace-20260310-0818.gz, trace-20260310-0820.gz).
comments: 2026-03-10 08:20 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Acknowledged. Opening incident and paging SRE. Contacted HelixBio to request traffic window info and ETA for a mitigation window.

2026-03-10 08:27 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Observed synchronous rise in rebalancer_cycle_count and queue_depth_per_pool. Initial hypothesis: rebalancer aggressively reallocated GPUs while a tenant produced many short-lived jobs, causing allocation thrash.
2026-03-10 08:33 - Customer (HelixBio - Lia Chen): Confirmed sudden surge of low-latency calls as part of a data-sync job. Reported elevated p99 and user-visible errors between 08:10-08:55 UTC.

2026-03-10 08:45 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Temporarily disabled automated rebalancer for pool-helix-3; pinned HelixBio's workloads to warm nodes as workaround. Observed queue depth drop within ~2 minutes and p99 latency reduced to ~150ms.

2026-03-11 10:05 - Platform Eng (Marta Iqbal): Collected allocation traces and started code-level reproduction in staging with synthetic short-job flood. Reproducer reproduces allocation churn at reduced scale.
2026-03-12 09:12 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Deployed rebalancer soft throttle patch to staging; scheduled canary to prod if metrics stable.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:00 - Correlation: rebalancer cycle timeouts increased from median 45ms to 320ms, concurrent with gpu_bind_latency and serving-runtime kvcache_evictions.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Hypothesis 1: Rebalancer does not account for short-job churn and treats transient allocation pressure as sustained, triggering unnecessary reallocations.

2026-03-10 10:40 - Hypothesis 2: Scheduler affinity heuristics allow noisy short jobs to preempt reserved allocations if they match GPU capability labels; need stronger reservation enforcement during rebalancer windows.
2026-03-11 11:30 - Traces: GPU allocation trace shows repeated allocate/release cycles for the same GPU within 30s windows for noisy-tenant-47 workloads.
2026-03-11 14:00 - Reproducer: Synthetic short-job flood + rebalancer cadence reproduces p99 spike in staging; adding a 15s minimum hold-time in rebalancer reduced churn in reproducer.
2026-03-12 08:00 - Data: 72% of allocation churn events were attributable to a single tenant's short burst traffic; remaining 28% were noise from background housekeeping jobs.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: Rebalancer was disabled for pool-helix-3 and HelixBio routes were pinned to a warm subset of GPUs. This reduced allocation churn and restored p99 latency to acceptable ranges.

Permanent fix plan: Merged PR to add a soft-throttle and minimum-hold-time to rebalancer logic (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rebalancer/pull/412). Changes: (1) rebalancer will require two consecutive cycle signals before reallocating a GPU, (2) backpressure window added to scheduler to deprioritize short-lived jobs during rebalancer windows, (3) stronger reservation enforcement for dedicated pools.

Rollout notes: Patch has been deployed to staging and will be rolled to a single canary reserved pool on 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC for 2 hours before broader rollout. Monitoring checks include allocation churn rate, p99 latency for pinned routes, and rebalancer_cycle_count.

Follow-up: Postmortem scheduled, and customer will be offered 10% credit for the degraded window as goodwill.
follow_up_actions: Add alert: rebalancer_cycle_count > 3/min for a given pool
Add alert: gpu_alloc_failures > 0.5% for reserved pools
Add scheduler change: short_job_sampling flag to avoid co-scheduling with reserved workloads
Run postmortem and update dedicated pool SLO docs
Plan customer communication and credit approval
